summary.headline: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed warrant articles for school roofs and capital projects while deferring votes on major road and water borrowing until Town Meeting.
summary.summary: At its March 18 meeting, the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed and voted on warrant recommendations for upcoming Annual Town Meeting articles. The committee unanimously recommended approval of non-bonded capital articles, water fund capital articles, school bonding items, and the MSBA-supported Trottier School roof replacement. However, members opted to defer recommendations on a $1 million water loop borrowing proposal and a multi-million-dollar road and sidewalk bonding plan to Town Meeting so they could obtain additional financial and cash-flow details.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved previous meeting minutes and handled administrative scheduling.
key_details: Approved minutes of January 5, 2026, as amended.
Approved minutes of March 9, 2026, as presented.

topics.title: FY27 capital request update: Atwood site remediation
topics.summary: The chair reported that the Select Board decided not to place the Atwood site remediation request, which involves a water tank, on the upcoming Annual Town Meeting warrant.
key_details: The project had been included on an earlier draft warrant.
Because it was removed from the warrant for this cycle, no immediate presentation or committee position is required.
topics.outcome: No action taken; deferred to a future cycle.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 9: Non-bonded general fund capital items
topics.summary: The committee reviewed capital items to be funded via levy, free cash, ambulance, or cemetery funds without borrowing. Members discussed the removal of a $75,000 van request, which was handled separately through the Advisory Committee's reserve fund as an emergency replacement, allowing overhead doors to remain in the article.
key_details: Funded through the operating budget levy, free cash, or dedicated reserves.
The $75,000 van was funded via reserve fund transfer and removed from the warrant article.
Overhead garage door replacements remain in the article.
topics.why_it_matters: Funding capital items via available town funds and levy impacts tax rates and annual department operations without incurring long-term borrowing debt.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 10: Water fund capital items
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and endorsed capital requests funded directly through the town's enterprise water fund rather than the general tax levy.
key_details: Paid directly by water ratepayers out of the water enterprise fund.
Does not impact the general tax levy or require municipal bonding.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 11: MWRA zero-percent loan for Fisher/Presidential loop
topics.summary: The committee reviewed an approximately $1 million borrowing article through the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority for a water main loop at Fisher Road and Presidential Drive to address water stagnation and pressure. Because of questions about water rate impacts and Select Board objections, the committee opted to withhold a recommendation until Town Meeting.
key_details: Estimated cost is approximately $1 million via a zero-percent interest loan through the MWRA.
Debt service would be repaid over roughly 10 years through water rates, not the tax levy.
The committee deferred its recommendation to Town Meeting to clarify the background behind the Select Board's split vote.
topics.outcome: Committee will report its position at Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The project impacts local water flow and pressure and is funded directly through water utility charges assessed to municipal water customers.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 12: School capital borrowing
topics.summary: The committee considered a borrowing article covering three school improvement projects across the Southborough public school district.
key_details: Includes Finn School classroom flooring, districtwide security system upgrades, and school technology infrastructure.
Requires a two-thirds majority vote at Town Meeting.
Does not require a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion ballot vote.
topics.why_it_matters: Finances long-term facility, security, and educational technology infrastructure across the town's schools.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 13: Road and sidewalk infrastructure bonding
topics.summary: The committee debated a major bonding authorization of up to $22 million to $25 million for road paving and sidewalk improvements. Members raised concerns that authorizing the full sum at once without detailed year-by-year cash flow and project rollout schedules could jeopardize Town Meeting approval, and voted to hold their recommendation until Town Meeting.
key_details: Authorizes borrowing of up to $22 million or more for comprehensive road paving and sidewalks based on an AI road-condition assessment.
Original discussions considered smaller initial tranches of roughly $5 million.
A committee member will coordinate with the Department of Public Works superintendent and the town accountant to map out multi-year contracting and debt projections.
topics.outcome: Committee will report its position at Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: A multi-million-dollar road authorization represents a major borrowing commitment that shapes municipal debt and roadway conditions across town for years.

topics.title: Town Meeting Article 15: Trottier School roof replacement borrowing
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the Trottier Middle School roof replacement project, which is partnered with the Massachusetts School Building Authority for state reimbursement.
key_details: Qualifies for an estimated 40-plus percent reimbursement from the MSBA.
Requires a two-thirds vote at Town Meeting as well as a majority vote for a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion at the May annual town election.
School officials reported the existing roof has experienced leaks since shortly after its original installation.
topics.why_it_matters: This multi-million-dollar school roof replacement requires a ballot-level debt exclusion that directly affects property tax bills over the term of the bond.

votes.motion: Support Article 9 (non-bonded capital items) as presented.
Support Article 10 (water fund capital items) as presented.
Support Article 12 (school capital bonding) as presented.
Support Article 15 (Trottier School roof replacement borrowing) as presented.

upcoming.what: Coordination between committee member, town accountant, and DPW superintendent on road bond scheduling
Annual Town Meeting and committee votes on Articles 11 and 13
Annual Town Election ballot vote on Trottier roof debt exclusion
